newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus pleased with British Midland deal.
newsitem.headline: Airbus pleased with British Midland deal.

text.p: European plane making consortium Airbus Industrie said an $1.0 billion order by British Midland for 20 aircraft was "very important" and showed the Airbus A320 family was a success.
A spokeswoman for the Toulouse-based group said that with British Midland, almost all British carriers were now using Airbus craft -- with the notable exception of British Airways Plc.
British Airways, which does operate some A320 planes it inherited from British Caledonian, is a very faithful client of The Boeing Co.
"We can't speak for BA or any other airline. But with 1,158 planes sold the A320 series shows to be a succesful plane which meets the needs of many operators," she said.
The British Midland deal is not included in the sales total because the order is not yet final - British Midland signed a memorandum of understanding.
The A320, started in 1988, is a short to medium haul aircraft with a single aisle and twin engines which seats 150 on average. Its price is about $47 million.
It was recently complemented by the smaller A319 which seats 124. The A321 is a stretch version and is worth around $54 million. It seats 186 passengers.

British Midland, which currently operates a fleet of 35 jet aircraft, will take delivery of eight A321s, 196-seat aircraft and twelve A320s, 160-seat aircraft phased over the next five years with three A321s entering service in Spring 1998.
Airbus currently builds 12 A320 planes per month.
Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
Aerospatiale and Deutsche Airbus have 38 pct each. British Aerospace Plc has 20 percent and CASA of Spain four percent.
